title: Homemade Mac MMO
author: LioDavinchy
selftext:
So I’ve been using AI for fun the last couple of years. I’ve been a hobby programmer my whole life. I’ve dabbled in all things software over the years. I learned maya and web design when they were new. I also played Mac games since sim ant and the original marathon.

Fast forward to today. I built a map software called LandNav world. It’s a Google Maps type map. While building it from scratch I built it around Apple technology like metal. I put in a feature I called game mode during development. It was a render engine to show the real world in 3D. It was just a side feature I used to allow walking on real trails as though you were at your local park.  It rendered so well I wondered if I could make a fork and put an actual game in it. I can and I am.

I loved the game shadowbane back in the day and I decided to build my game around the concept of an open world MMO. Something like this before AI would be literally impossible for a single person. I know how to model 3d models. I know how to code a simple engine. I know how to create images and textures in photoshop. Any one of those things would take a team of people years to create even simple assets for a game.  Turns out Claude did it in a week.

From experience with mmo betas over the years my current game is beyond many of the alphas I’ve played. I’d guess in another week I’ll have a playable game. I’ve developed for apple silicon Mac’s and iOS devices. I’m testing on an m1 air. It’s been really fun developing the AI tools to make this happen. A lot of the base ideas exist but not for full AI production. The 3D tools can make models but not for games. The armor is taking custom software to make the models adaptable to bending.  There is now motion capture tech that can use an iPhone video to create motion capture that blockbuster video producers would have drooled for 20 years ago.

I know a lot of people hate AI and call anything produced by it slop. I know there is a lot of garbage out there but it is fun to see ideas you have, brought to life in minutes instead of years.  There will now be an mmo on Mac that maybe a handful of people will get a kick out of. I’ll post a link when it’s playable.
